title: The Antisemitic Forgery That Copied Another Book

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: The supposed secret document was fake. And partly copied.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: It’s called The Protocols of the Elders of Zion. First published in nineteen-oh-three, it pretended to reveal secret Jewish plans.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: But those meeting records were invented. And here’s the giveaway: large sections came from an earlier French political satire that wasn’t even about Jewish people.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: In nineteen-twenty-one, The Times of London exposed the copying. The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum documents the forgery and how it kept spreading afterward.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: So this wasn’t a hidden truth finally uncovered. It was a fabricated accusation dressed up as an insider document. A dramatic cover didn’t make it evidence.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: That matters when a post recycles the same story with new graphics. New packaging doesn’t repair false evidence.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: An old lie doesn’t become true in high definition.
scenes.on_screen: AN OLD LIE ISN'T TRUE IN HIGH DEFINITION
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
